rationale: This article conducts a doctrinal legal and policy analysis of international human rights law and Australian Commonwealth water law concerning the recognition of First Nations women's voices and holistic rights to use and manage water according to First Nations law, illustrated by two legal case studies. It does not present primary empirical evidence or a systematic review (E05), and its subject matter and evaluated outcomes concern Indigenous water resource management and legal governance recognition rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the literal/plain Criterion 2 wording, the article examines international human rights law and Australian Commonwealth water law and policy (c2_legal_admin_plain = yes), whereas under the 2026-10-13 narrow reading it focuses on holistic water resource governance and legal recognition rather than a legal/regulatory mechanism governing household or community water/sanitation service access (c2_legal_admin_narrow = no). Both decisions remain exclude because it is a doctrinal legal analysis (E05) focused on Indigenous water resource management and participatory recognition rather than empirical household/community service access outcomes.
